$generated_by: manual (14 May 2026, Victor + Claude) — single source of truth for endpoint sync cadence
$how_to_use: Each entry maps a v1 endpoint path prefix to its upstream data source, the sync script that refreshes it, and the cadence tier. The audit_endpoint_docs.py script uses this file to inject a 'Data freshness' line into every endpoint description. brubru-cron-sync (Railway) reads this file to dispatch the right script at the right time.

live_passthrough.description: No cache — the endpoint hits the upstream source on every request.
live_passthrough.freshness_label: Live pass-through (no cache; hits upstream on every request).

hot_6h.description: Refreshed 4 times per day. For time-sensitive sources where same-day freshness is a conversion lever.

warm_12h.description: Refreshed twice a day. For sources that move daily but where half-day lag is acceptable.

daily.description: Refreshed once per night. For sources that move a few times per week.
daily.freshness_label: Synced once per day at 04:00 UTC from {source}.

economy_daily.description: v2 institutional/agency/database endpoints (economy_items). Refreshed daily, batched across 10:00 / 15:00 / 21:00 UTC to spread scraper load over ~34 EU bodies.
economy_daily.freshness_label: Synced once per day (10:00 / 15:00 / 21:00 UTC, batched by body) from {source}.

weekly.description: Refreshed once per week. For slow-moving universes (FTAs, GIs, vocabularies).
weekly.freshness_label: Synced once per week (Sunday 03:00 UTC) from {source}.

monthly.description: Refreshed once per month. For corpora and release cycles (LEG bulk, EU Vocabularies releases).
monthly.freshness_label: Synced once per month (1st of month, 02:00 UTC) from {source}.

manual.description: No automated sync. Backfilled on user request via CLI.
manual.freshness_label: Backfilled manually via CLI (no automated cron). Last full backfill: see ingestion notes.
